reason: The question was the most important thing to get right this week, and the draft gets it right. It gives a clear "no" to doubling from 40 to 80 miles and to running twice a day, and it explains why: there isn't enough time left to build volume, and a jump that size is a major injury risk. Next week adds up to about 47 miles, which is reasonable after this week's 40 and below the 53-mile peak, so there's no sharp jump in weekly volume. The plan keeps Marisol's usual pattern: Monday and Friday off, a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday. Every day has a distance and a pace or heart-rate cap, so it can be run as written. The heavy legs early in the week cleared by Thursday, so this isn't pain, illness or exhaustion, and no other must-never check is triggered. What keeps it from a 5: the long run goes from 15 to 20 miles with the last 8 at goal pace, and the week also has a 6-mile goal-pace session on Wednesday. For a peak week that's a lot. It's probably fine given the 53-mile week before, but it's at the edge. The draft also mentions things that aren't on the card, such as "5 weeks to go", "executed exactly as written" and "effort 5/10". It doesn't mention the heavy legs at all.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You executed the week exactly as written and the long run came in strong at effort 5/10, so with 5 weeks to go we push…
Answers: (1) No, do not double to 80 miles or add doubles. You are 5 weeks from the start line, not 5 months, and the window for building volume has closed. (2) Jumping from 40 to 80 in one week is roughly the single biggest predictor of injury I can name. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to absorb Sunday's 15.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Shakes the long run out of the legs.
Wed: quality, 10 mi with 2 x 3 mi at 8:35/mi, 3 min jog between. Second dose of goal…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145. Recovery after the hard day, keep it…
Fri: rest. Protect Sunday's long run.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Legs loose for tomorrow, not a mile faster than…
Sun: long, 20 mi with the last 8 at 8:35/mi, first 12 at 9:50 to 10:00/mi. The key…
